title: Unified Responses Translation Proxy (PoC) — preserve streaming + function calls + structured output
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Proof-of-concept for a lightweight translation proxy that accepts upstream OpenAI Responses API traffic and emits equivalent Redwood internal events, preserving streaming boundaries, tool/function call semantics, and structured output hints. The proxy is intended to reduce customer migration friction for partners using the OpenAI Responses surface while avoiding invasive changes to runtime kernels.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy can accept a streamed OpenAI Responses session and translate into Redwood streaming frames with matching ordering semantics
Tool/function call start/complete events are mapped 1:1 and trigger existing function routing in Dedicated/Private deployments
Structured output markers (json_schema, modalities) are surfaced to downstream eval/quality hooks
Lossiness budget documented and demonstrated via regression tests for 3 canonical scenarios: tool call interleaving, partial structured output emission, and interrupted streams
End-to-end latency overhead of the proxy <= 8ms median for small payloads in hosting environment
Automated contract tests against an OpenAI Responses fixture pass in CI (smoke + fuzzed event orderings)
tasks: Draft design doc: translation format, event watermarking, token provenance headers
Implement minimal HTTP/1.1 streaming server that ingests events and emits Redwood frames
Mapping layer for function call lifecycle: start -> call -> result/error
Implement structured-output guards: JSON schema hint passthrough and strict-mode fallback
Write contract test harness and a small fuzzer for event reordering
Benchmark latency and measure p50/p95 overhead against direct runtime path
Security review for header forwarding and KMS token handling
discussion: 2025-02-11 — Ayesha Patel: Kickoff — PoC scope agreed: only translation of streaming/responses events, no model-level rerouting in PoC. Keep it as an opt-in gateway behind a feature flag.

2025-02-12 — Marco Liang: Implementation note — We'll use an event buffer with explicit watermarking so that we can reconcile tool-call boundaries without blocking on token finality. Proposed watermark strategy: event-id + last-stable-offset.
2025-02-14 — Priya Desai (PM): Concern — customers expect 1:1 fidelity for function call ordering. We should quantify where the proxy may reorder events and document the behavioral contract.

2025-02-15 — Eng review (Ravi Kumar): Suggestion — embed a provenance header (X-RW-Source-Token-IDs) to allow downstream tracing of tokens to upstream frames for audits and QA. Also recommended backpressure propagation to upstream clients.

2025-02-17 — Design feedback (Leah Gomez): For structured outputs, add an optional strict-emit mode that fails the response if the schema is violated; default to a best-effort mode to avoid breaking existing usage.

2025-02-18 — Marco Liang: Progress — core proxy stub implemented. Basic streaming replay + tool call mapping green in local harness. Opening WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/2124
2025-02-19 — Security (Olaf Svensson): Note — must ensure we do not log tool payloads. Marking sensitive headers for redaction in the proxy and gating access to token provenance mapping via RBAC.
decision_log: Decision 2025-02-12: Use watermarking buffer instead of synchronous token accumulation to balance latency vs fidelity.
Decision 2025-02-14: PoC will not modify model routing or perform cross-model fallback. The proxy only translates events into the existing runtime API.
Decision 2025-02-17: Add 'strict-emit' config flag for structured outputs. Default remains 'best-effort' to minimize breakage.
Decision 2025-02-18: Include X-RW-Source-Token-IDs header for token-level debugging but gate via RBAC and do not store in logs by default.
test_plan: Unit tests for mapping logic: tool-call events, content-chunk events, end-of-stream markers
Contract tests using 10k synthetic sessions with injected reorderings and dropped frames
Integration smoke: deploy PoC behind feature flag in staging and run 50k short-chat requests
Security tests: verify redaction of sensitive headers and no persistent storage of raw tool payloads
rollout_plan: Phase 0: PoC in staging behind feature-flaged ingress for internal partner accounts
Phase 1: Canary in hosted with small traffic % and telemetry collection for mismatch rates
Phase 2: Expand to Dedicated trials with explicit customer opt-in and SLA guardrails
Rollback: disable feature flag and drain active proxied sessions; instrument alert for mismatch > 0.5%
notes: Trade-offs: The proxy reduces migration work for customers but adds another hop that can introduce subtle ordering differences under high contention. The watermarking approach trades a small bounded delay for stronger function-call boundary guarantees.
Future work: Explore native runtime-side support to accept OpenAI Responses v2-format natively (long-term), collapse the proxy, and remove the translation cost.

Known limitations in PoC: does not support multi-model fanout, partial message edits, or token-level deterministic replay across quantized runtimes. These are out-of-scope for initial proof-of-concept.
